risk: Goal hijack by direct prompt injection
description: A customer types instructions that override the agent's purpose and make it reveal data or take unintended actions.
cause: Instructions and data share one text channel; the model follows persuasive text.

description: Hidden instructions in a document, email text or tool result steer the agent while the customer sees nothing odd.
cause: Agent reads untrusted content (retrieved documents, tool output, attachments).

description: The agent calls an allowed tool with harmful parameters, for example freezing the wrong card or sending a large number of requests.
cause: Tool scope is broad; parameters are decided by the model.

risk: Cross-customer access through the agent (confused deputy)
description: The agent uses its own broad rights to fetch another customer's data because the request looks valid.
cause: Authorisation is checked against the agent, not the end user.
note: Low likelihood is conditional on G-02 being enforced at the tool server, not only at the edge

description: A long-lived token for a tool server leaks and is used outside the agent.
cause: Standing secrets, shared service accounts, secrets in config or logs.

risk: Compromised model, tool server or prompt template
description: A tool server, MCP server, library or hosted model changes behaviour through a malicious or careless update.
cause: Dynamic components are pulled in without pinning or verification; provider changes are not noticed.

description: A tool or generated output causes code or commands to run in the agent's environment.
cause: Tools that evaluate text or run code; weak input validation.

description: False or malicious content is stored in session memory or shared state and later treated as trusted.
cause: Memory writes from untrusted content; no isolation or expiry.

description: A forged or altered message between the coordinator and a specialist triggers an action.
cause: Agents trust each other's text; no sender authentication.

risk: Cascading failure, runaway loop or cost spike
description: An error in one agent spreads to others, or a loop consumes budget and capacity.
cause: No step or budget limits; shared state spreads errors.

description: Customers act on a confident wrong answer, or staff approve Tier 3 requests without looking (approval fatigue, automation bias).
cause: Fluent output; many routine approvals; summaries written by the agent.
note: Hardest to reduce by technology alone; depends on training and sampling

description: Behaviour moves away from the intended scope over time, for example after a model update, without anyone noticing.
cause: Provider model changes; no behavioural monitoring.

risk: Personal or financial data leaks to the model provider, logs or replies
description: Account details are sent to a third party, written to logs in clear, or appear in another person's reply.
cause: Raw text sent to models; verbose logging; weak output checks.

risk: Wrong financial information stated as fact
description: The agent invents a fee, a right or a product term and the customer relies on it, leading to complaints or mis-selling findings.
cause: Model generates plausible text without a source.

description: Product teams add credit-limit, loan-eligibility or insurance features, making the system high-risk under Annex III without a new assessment.
cause: Business pressure; classification treated as a one-time memo.
affected_parties: Customers (decisions about credit or insurance), the firm
note: Impact is regulatory: obligations of Arts 8-27 apply from the Annex III date

description: Customers are not clearly told they are talking to AI, or the agent behaves as if it were a person.
cause: Design choices that favour a human feel; disclosure removed in a UI change.

risk: Model provider outage or terms change
description: The hosted model is unavailable, degraded or its terms change, interrupting customer service.
cause: Single-provider dependency.

risk: Insufficient evidence to reconstruct an incident
description: After an incident the firm cannot show what the agent did, for whom, or why, and cannot answer a regulator.
cause: Missing or inconsistent logs; short retention; clocks out of sync.

risk: Unfair or poor service for some customers
description: Service quality is worse for certain languages, accents, accessibility needs or vulnerable customers.
cause: Model performance differs across groups; no testing for it.
affected_parties: Customers with particular needs or languages
note: No fairness or bias evaluation is designed (NIST MEASURE 2.11 is a stated gap), so residual stays medium until one is added

description: A prompt, tool list or approval rule is changed without review, silently altering behaviour.
cause: Weak change control; excessive privileged access.
